we have found efficient first-order model-checking algorithms for every first-order property that can be expressed by a first-order formula, and every first-order counting query, in every class of bounded expansion, and in every nicely locally tree-decomposed class of graphs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the first-order model checking problem can be solved efficiently in many classes of graphs that are not necessarily of bounded tree-width.

first-order logic can be used for efficient model-checking in classes of graphs of bounded local tree-width and bounded arboricity, and for counting queries in classes of graphs with bounded expansion.
